title: Windows artifact and moe CLI
description: Objective: an installable Windows artifact - unzip, moe init, moe start. Measured at HEAD 1aa7cdc: no pack/build/dist script exists anywhere (root package.json:13-32); tsconfig.base.json:13 noEmit - the daemon runs as plain node on .ts sources (Node >=24.16 <25 type-stripping, 628 export-star .js bridges satisfy nodenext resolution); apps/daemon bin entries point at raw .ts (package.json:7-11) but the package is private:true; daemon external dep closure is exactly ONE package (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk - store uses node:sqlite); root node_modules is 543M. tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts (Ed25519 container/manifest) exists but is wired to no pack command. Deliverable: (a) a thin moe CLI bin (new file; init = scaffold store dir + mint operator credential + write config; start = compose the moe-up launcher from this epic's task 1); (b) a pack script producing a zip via pnpm deploy of @moe/daemon (prunes to the 1-external-dep closure) + control-room vite build static output + the CLI + a README; (c) a clean-machine smoke: unzip on a machine/dir without the repo, moe init, moe start, daemon origin reachable. Node 24.16 is a documented prerequisite (no bundled runtime in v0.1). NOT in scope: npm publication (license pending - separate BACKLOG task), code signing, auto-update, bundling node. Depends on: moe up launcher task (same epic). Verification: pack script exits 0, zip size reported, clean-dir smoke from PowerShell passes.
definitionOfDone: pnpm run pack (or equivalent) produces a zip containing the daemon closure, CLI, and built control-room; the script exits 0 and prints the artifact path and size.

On a clean directory outside the repo: unzip, moe init (creates store + credential + config with named refusals on bad input), moe start (daemon + wrapper up, origin printed) - asserted by the PowerShell smoke.
The zip contains no dev dependencies, no tests, no .git, and node_modules is the pruned deploy closure, asserted by an inventory check in the pack script.
pnpm typecheck exits 0; pack/CLI tests pass with a nonzero Test Files count line; only explicit owned paths committed.
taskRails: Hard dependency: the moe up launcher task in this epic; the CLI start command composes it, never reimplements process management.
No compilation step; ship .ts sources + .js bridges as-is on the documented Node 24.16 prerequisite.
Credentials are minted at init, never shipped in the artifact; the smoke asserts the artifact contains no credential bytes.
Windows-first; run all smokes from PowerShell, not Git Bash.

implementationPlan.note:
THE REJECT FIX. TDD order: sweep test written first, RED with 6 failures naming exactly the shapes QA found, then the matcher.

WHAT I MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING (all four QA issues reproduced):
`isTestArtifact` shipped 26 repo-owned test artifacts (QA's 25 + packages/runner/src/supervisor/race-harness.ts, which the reject did not list). Vendored: 65 node_modules files sit under a `tests/` segment, so a global segment rule would have STRIPPED the published closure the same DoD clause requires — the widened rules are therefore scoped to non-`node_modules` paths, and there is a test pinning both directions.

1. MATCHER (pack-inventory.ts). Suffix TABLE replaced by whole-basename rules: `(^|[.-_])fixtures?\.`, `(^|[.-_])harness\.`, `(^|[.-_])test-(helpers?|data|utils?)\.`, `\.(test|spec)\.`, plus DIRECTORY segments `test`/`tests` (segment, never substring — `native/src/spec.rs` is production `mod spec;` in lib.rs and must survive).

2. THE TRAP QA NAMED. `.js` forms widened in the same edit, so `admission-fixtures.js` cannot survive a prune that deletes `admission-fixtures.ts`.

3. WHAT PRUNING MORE BROKE, AND THE PROOF THAT IT NO LONGER DOES. Widening alone leaves 5 shipped survivors importing a deleted module (`race-scenarios.ts -> ./effect-test-fixtures.js` and 4 more) — and the OLD artifact already shipped those 5 broken edges. New gate `PACK_DANGLING_IMPORT` + `PACK_DEV_DEPENDENCY_IMPORT` (`collectImportFaults`) scans every shipped source: a relative import with no target, or an import of a dev-only package (two files import `vitest`), refuses the pack by name. That is the completeness proof for `TEST_SUPPORT_STEMS`, the 10 test-support files whose FILENAME says nothing (each verified test-only by listing every importer: all `*.test.ts` or each other). Miss one and the pack stops; it cannot ship silently.

4. `removeEmptyDirectories`: Compress-Archive stores directory entries, so the emptied `native/tests/` still listed in the zip. Removed bottom-up, count logged.

comments.content: PACKAGING CAVEATS from independent review 2026-08-18 (verified: all 3 bins import clean on plain Node 24 in 446ms; dep closure = @modelcontextprotocol/sdk only). For the plan: (1) the sdk fans out to 39 transitive packages including express 5 and zod 4 — that IS the audit surface of the artifact; the pack inventory check should list the closure so it is reviewed, not discovered. (2) `engines` is pinned only at the ROOT package.json — the packed @moe/daemon manifest carries no engines field, so the artifact's own manifest (or the moe CLI at startup) must enforce Node >=24.16 <25 with a named refusal, or a Node 22 user gets a cryptic type-stripping syntax error instead. (3) The runtime layout is load-bearing twice: 628 export-star .js bridges AND pnpm's node_modules symlink structure — `pnpm deploy` preserves both, but the zip step must not flatten symlinks into copies that break peer resolution, and the clean-machine smoke is what proves it survived. (4) Add a `moe-wrapper` bin entry for agent-wrapper-main.ts alongside the existing three while touching the bin map — agent-wrapper-main has no bin today, and the packed CLI's start command should not hardcode a src path into another package's internals.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

TEST_SEGMENTS is only ['__tests__','__mocks__'], so a plain 'tests/' directory is invisible and 10 Rust test files ship: packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/tests/{containment,descriptor_block,frame_sweep,handle_inheritance,idempotence,node_loadability,session}.rs and .../native/tests/{job_sweep,process_sweep,real_windows}.rs. The case 'refuses shipped test fixtures, which a *.test.ts filter alone would miss' uses exactly one path, claude-launcher-test-fixtures.ts, which the suffix list already catches. It establishes nothing about the shapes in the tree: I simulated isTestArtifact and it returns true for that path and false for test-fixtures.ts, admission-fixtures.ts, journal-test-harness.ts and native/tests/job_sweep.rs. Replace it with a sweep over the real file list, asserting the swept case count is NONZERO.
